title: Soft SLO signal fuse and graceful deferment hotfix
author: Leah Kim
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce a short 'SLO signal fuse' to prevent repeat reopen/flip-flop in circuit state
Behavioral change: per-tenant defer window added (non-breaking, configurable)
Telemetry: new metric slo.suppress.count and alert thresholds added
body:
Motivation: During a regional degradation on 2026-02-26 (SUP-847) we observed rapid circuit reopen/close oscillation for several tenants which amplified downstream KV pressure and caused transient SLO violations. This hotfix introduces a short-lived 'SLO signal fuse' and a configurable per-tenant deferment policy to stabilize circuit transitions and avoid repeated soft-reopens in noisy environments.

Summary of changes (single line description): add slo signal fuse, tenant-level defer window, tighter telemetry and canary rollout knobs; cherry-pick to release branch for fast remediation.

What this fixes: prevents oscillation loops where health probes flip circuit state repeatedly within the same control epoch; reduces duplicate warm-up of KV caches and lowers incidence of transient latency spikes.

Design and rationale:
- SLO signal fuse: a short-duration suppression window (default 45s) during which repeated SLO-triggered reopen attempts are suppressed. This is conservative and intended only for short noisy bursts.
- Per-tenant defer window: tenants can be assigned defer windows to avoid repeated canary reassigns during recovery. Configurable via runtime flags and surfaced in Console.
- Telemetry: emit slo.suppress.count, slo.fuse.active, and slo.defer.window_millis for observability and postmortem analysis.
- Canary rollout: staged to 10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic with metric gates (95th p90 latency, failed_reopen_rate).

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for fuse timer, defer map, and config parsing
- [x] Integration test for reopen suppression (flaky repro captured and stabilized)
- [x] Added metrics and Grafana dashboard snippet for quick ops view
- [x] Canary plan and rollback instructions included in PR body
- [x] Cherry-pick prepared for release/2026-03-01

Commits summary:
- 8f2a7c3: hotfix(slo): add slo signal fuse core logic + unit tests
- 2b9d11e: runtime: expose per-tenant defer window and default config
- 7c3e2b1: telemetry: add slo.suppress.count and dashboard query snippet
- d1a9b0f: ci: stabilize slo_reopen_integration test and add flakiness tag

Changed areas (high-level):
- runtime/slo/fuse.go: new fuse implementation and tests
- runtime/slo/defer_map.go: per-tenant defer window management
- runtime/config/defaults.go: new default values and flags
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go: added metrics and tags
- infra/canary/plan.yaml: canary rollout steps and gating thresholds
- tests/integration/slo_reopen_test.go: improved determinism and assertions
- docs/ops/slo-fuse.md: operational runbook and remediation steps
- console/api/tenant_config.go: expose defer window knob via admin API

Review conversation (high level):
- Diego Morales (2026-03-01): "Nice safe approach. A couple of questions: how did we pick 45s? Could this hide a persistent failure and delay remediation?"
- Leah Kim (reply 2026-03-01): "45s is conservative and chosen from historic reopen storm traces — we also gate with a separate 'failed_reopen_rate' metric that will trigger an immediate open when sustained errors are observed. I'll add this explanation to the comments and doc."
- Priya Sharma (2026-03-01): "Please ensure the console UI surfaces the active fuse state per-tenant. Ops would like quick visibility."
- Leah Kim (reply 2026-03-01): "console/api changes included; dashboard snippet added. Fuse state exported as slo.fuse.active tag for tenant filters."
- Elias Novak (2026-03-02): "Integration test initially flaky in CI — looks like a timing race. Suggest increasing test timeouts and adding deterministic clock for unit tests."
- Leah Kim (reply 2026-03-02): "Applied deterministic clock in tests and bumped integration window; CI green after rerun."
- Priya Sharma (approval 2026-03-02): "Approved for hotfix roll — recommend monitoring for 24h post-merge."

CI summary:
- build: pass
- unit tests: pass (deterministic clock fixes applied)
- integration: initially failed (slo_reopen_integration) -> rerun -> pass
- lint: pass
- e2e smoke: pass on canary stage

Canary plan (concise):
- Stage 1: 10% traffic for 30m; watch slo.fuse.active and failed_reopen_rate; abort if failed_reopen_rate > 0.5% or p95 latency increases by >10%
- Stage 2: 50% traffic for 30m; same gates
- Stage 3: 100% traffic and backfill metrics

Rollback instructions: revert to previous release tag in orchestration; clear defer_map entries if needed to remove tenant stickiness; run fail-open script (ops/run-failopen.sh) in emergency.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged to release/2026-03-01 via squash merge by Leah Kim (2026-03-02). Hotfix cherry-picked to main for follow-up stability improvements.

Post-merge actions:
- Ops runbook posted (docs/ops/slo-fuse.md) and pinned in #sre-alerts
- Pager duty runbook updated with new alert slo.suppress.count > 20/min for > 5m
- Follow-up work: ENG-4217 to evaluate adaptive fuse duration and SRE-983 to audit tenant defer assignments
